assertion_audit.failure_condition: Switching the initial journal to WAL or another non-delete mode fails this assertion.
Not applying the declared busy timeout to SQLite fails this assertion; the next literal 120.0 assertion independently fixes the intended bound.
Changing the declared timeout away from 120 seconds fails this independent literal assertion.
Dropping or duplicating a hot or retired input row fails the expected cardinality check.

assertion_audit.assertion: assert {row["run_id"] for row in expected} == {row["run_id"] for row in rows}
assertion_audit.failure_condition: Returning the wrong identities despite the same cardinality fails the fixture identity-set check.
The controller failing to release the consumer within 15 seconds fails this synchronization assertion and is propagated through errors.

assertion_audit.assertion: assert consuming.wait(10), "reader did not reach record consumption"
assertion_audit.failure_condition: The reader never reaching the patched normalization consumer fails the start barrier.

assertion_audit.assertion: assert thread.is_alive(), "read consumption ended before the write receipt"
assertion_audit.failure_condition: The reader finishing or its synchronization failing before the subprocess receipt fails the overlap assertion.

Restoring yield from connection.execute keeps the read cursor live during the pause, so the separate writer exceeds its one-second busy timeout and this returncode assertion fails; all three recorded negative-control cases do so.
The subprocess not retrieving the inserted record, or returning another identity, fails the JSON receipt check; stdout comes from get_run, not directly from its input literal.
The reader hanging after release fails the bounded join check.
A reader exception, including a failed release barrier, fails the captured errors check.

The concurrent read differing in fields or row membership from its uncontended read fails the snapshot comparison; identity and cardinality are independently anchored above, while this assertion claims concurrency equivalence rather than a complete external semantics oracle.
The committed concurrent row not surviving subprocess exit fails the fresh-connection readback.
The journal mode changing during the exercise fails the final rollback-mode check.

assertion_independence: No added assertion is invariant under restoring the live-cursor regression: returncode exposes it. The timeout comparison is tied to configuration but anchored by the separate 120.0 literal; read equality is intentionally between two separate executions with and without a concurrent writer, anchored by fixture IDs and count.
